name: obol_flag_hunt_2026_09
description: Thorough post-foothold flag capture, split the way the exam scores it: the LOCAL/user flag from any shell, and the ROOT/proof flag once you have administrative access. Each flag is captured next to a host-identity command (for the screenshot) and recorded as its own objective, so grabbing the user flag never hides the still-open root flag.

source.name: O.B.O.L flag capture methodology
source.notes: A captured flag is proof, not a checkbox. Local and root are separate objectives (objective.local_flag / objective.root_flag) so the coach keeps prompting for the one you have not captured yet.

actions.title: Capture the User Flag (Linux)
actions.hypothesis: ANY Linux shell can read the user flag - a reverse shell or webshell reads user.txt/local.txt as readily as an SSH login, no credential required. Grab it first and mark the local objective done; the root flag is its own step once you escalate.

report.finding: Captured the local/user flag from the Linux foothold.

commands.note: SSH INTERACTIVE SHELL (When port 22 is open and credentials are known): Log in directly to an interactive shell on the target host.
ENABLE SSH KEY LOGIN (From remote command execution): Authorize your Kali SSH public key on the target account so you can SSH in interactively.
REVERSE SHELL UPGRADE (From one-shot remote execution): Catch an interactive shell on your Kali listener (`nc -lvnp {{lport}}`).

IN YOUR SHELL (no credential needed): find every flag file and print the user flag with your identity for the screenshot. The common case - you do not need SSH creds to read a flag you can already reach.
commands.run: whoami; id; hostname; ip -4 addr | grep inet; find / -xdev -type f -size -4k \( {{flag_inames_linux}} \) 2>/dev/null -exec echo '--- {} ---' \; -exec cat {} \;

commands.note: LOCATE OVER SSH (only if you hold SSH creds and have no shell yet). A one-liner from Kali, so it only LOCATES; OffSec scores a flag read this way ZERO. Paste the output back and obol records the path; capture it on the host next.

ON THE HOST, capture the LOCAL/user flag with its identity. Run this INSIDE your shell and screenshot the whole frame: whoami + id + ip addr (the target IP) + the flag, together. obol records this as the captured local flag.
commands.run: whoami; id; hostname; ip -4 addr | grep inet; cat {{flag_path_local}}

commands.note: REMOTE SSH PROOF READ (from Kali): Run id, hostname, ip addr, and cat the located user flag over SSH via NetExec.
commands.run: nxc ssh {{target}} -u '{{user}}' -p '{{password}}' -x 'id; hostname; ip -4 addr | grep inet; cat {{flag_path_local}}'

actions.title: Capture the Root Flag (Linux)
actions.hypothesis: You have root - capture the proof flag before anything else so you can mark the box's final objective done. It lives in /root, which only root can read; grab it with your identity for the screenshot, then move on (persistence, pivot, loot) knowing the box is owned.

report.finding: Captured the root/proof flag from the Linux host.

commands.note: ROOT SSH INTERACTIVE SHELL (When port 22 is open): Connect directly to an interactive root shell over SSH.
AUTHORIZE ROOT SSH KEY (From remote command execution): Plant your Kali SSH public key into /root/.ssh/authorized_keys to open an interactive root SSH session.
ROOT REVERSE SHELL UPGRADE (From remote command execution): Catch an interactive root shell on your Kali listener (`nc -lvnp {{lport}}`).
IN YOUR ROOT SHELL: locate the root/proof flag and print it alongside your root identity and IP address for the report screenshot.
commands.run: whoami; id; hostname; ip -4 addr | grep inet; find / -xdev -type f -size -4k \( {{flag_inames_linux}} \) 2>/dev/null -exec echo '--- {} ---' \; -exec cat {} \;

commands.note: ON THE HOST as root, capture the ROOT flag with its identity. Run this INSIDE your root shell and screenshot the whole frame together (id must show uid=0). obol records this as the captured root flag - the box's final objective.
commands.run: whoami; id; hostname; ip -4 addr | grep inet; cat {{flag_path_root}}

commands.note: COMBINED USER + ROOT PROOF READ (In-Session): Print host identity, IP, local flag, and root flag in one terminal frame when both paths have been located.
commands.run: whoami; id; hostname; ip -4 addr | grep inet; cat {{flag_path_local}}; cat {{flag_path_root}}

commands.note: REMOTE SSH LOCATE (from Kali): Search /root for the root/proof flag over SSH via NetExec when root SSH credentials are known.
REMOTE SSH PROOF READ (from Kali): Run id, hostname, ip addr, and cat the located root flag over SSH via NetExec.
commands.run: nxc ssh {{target}} -u '{{user}}' -p '{{password}}' -x 'id; hostname; ip -4 addr | grep inet; cat {{flag_path_root}}'

actions.title: Capture the User Flag (Windows)
actions.hypothesis: ANY Windows shell reads the user flag - a webshell, a WinRM session, or a service-exploit shell all read the user's Desktop\local.txt, no credential required. Grab it first and mark the local objective done; the root/proof flag is its own step once you are SYSTEM/Administrator.

report.finding: Captured the local/user flag from the Windows foothold.

commands.note: WINRM INTERACTIVE SHELL (Recommended when port 5985 is open): Connect directly over WinRM with domain credentials. Once connected, locate and capture the user flag.
WINRM PASS-THE-HASH SHELL: Connect directly over WinRM with a captured NT hash.
RDP INTERACTIVE DESKTOP (When port 3389 is open): Open a full interactive RDP desktop session on the target host.
PORT 135/445 WMI INTERACTIVE SHELL (When WinRM 5985 is closed): Spawns a semi-interactive C:\> prompt over WMI and SMB.
PORT 445 INTERACTIVE SYSTEM SHELL: Spawns an interactive command prompt over SMB.
PORT 445 SMBEXEC SHELL: Opens a semi-interactive SYSTEM shell over port 445 without dropping a service binary on disk.

commands.note: ENABLE WINRM / RDP GROUP ACCESS (When direct login is blocked or ports 3389/5985 are closed): Grants your user Remote Management Users and Remote Desktop Users membership and enables RDP & WinRM. Paste the output back to unlock xfreerdp and evil-winrm.
commands.web_note: ENABLE RDP & WINRM REMOTELY: Adds your user to Remote Desktop Users and Remote Management Users and enables RDP (3389) and WinRM (5985). Paste output back to unlock xfreerdp and evil-winrm.

commands.note: REVERSE SHELL UPGRADE: Execute from a one-shot command runner or service to catch an interactive shell on your Kali listener (`nc -lvnp {{lport}}`).
UNIVERSAL IN-SESSION LOCATE (Works in both CMD/wmiexec/psexec/smbexec and PowerShell/Evil-WinRM): Sweep all user Desktops for the user/local flag file in under 1 second.
commands.web_note: STEP 2 (Inside your on-host shell): Locate the user flag across all user profile Desktops. Paste the path it prints to fill the proof read command below.

commands.note: IN-SESSION POWERSHELL LOCATE (For PS C:\> shells like Evil-WinRM): Inside your interactive shell, recursively search user profiles to verify the exact path of the user flag. Paste the path it prints and obol fills the read below.

UNIVERSAL IN-SESSION PROOF READ (Works in both CMD/wmiexec/psexec/smbexec and PowerShell/Evil-WinRM): Display whoami, hostname, ipconfig, and the located user flag in one command frame for the report screenshot.
commands.web_note: STEP 3 (Inside your on-host shell): Display whoami, hostname, ipconfig, and the user flag in a single command frame.

commands.note: IN-SESSION POWERSHELL PROOF READ (For PS C:\> shells like Evil-WinRM or powershell.exe): Display user identity (whoami), host identity (hostname), IP (ipconfig), and the located user flag in the same frame for the report screenshot.
WINRM REMOTE LOCATE (When port 5985 is open): Search user profiles for the user flag remotely over WinRM in one command without opening an interactive shell.
commands.run: nxc winrm {{target}} -u '{{user}}' -p '{{password}}' -x 'Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users -Filter *user.txt -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty FullName'

commands.note: WINRM REMOTE READ (When port 5985 is open): Read the confirmed user flag directly over WinRM in one shot from Kali.
WINRM REMOTE READ WITH NT HASH: Read the confirmed user flag over WinRM using pass-the-hash.
LOCATE OVER SMB (from Kali): Spiders the Users share to discover the exact path of the user/local flag file before reading it.
commands.web_note: WHY REMOTE SMB right now: Standard domain users cannot open an interactive shell when WinRM (5985) and RDP (3389) are closed. Spidering the Users share locates user.txt now; once you escalate to Administrator (e.g. Kerberoasting), Capture the Root/Proof Flag provides an On-Host Shell command to capture both user.txt and root.txt on-host with whoami/hostname/ipconfig.

commands.note: SMB SHARE CAPTURE (Ungates once the flag path is located on the Users share): Downloads and prints the located user flag from the discovered share path.
commands.web_note: REMOTE SMB CAPTURE: Downloads user.txt from the discovered Users share path. Once you obtain Administrator access, use On-Host Shell on the Root/Proof Flag card to capture your on-host proof screenshot for both user.txt and root.txt.

commands.note: REMOTE LOCATE OVER SMB: Searches every user profile Desktop over SMB. Note: Requires administrative execution rights on the target; if execution fails on non-admin accounts, use evil-winrm.

LAB QUICK GRAB (not OffSec-legal): with the dumped Administrator hash, search every user's Desktop and print the flag remotely in one shot, no shell. obol fills the hash from the NTDS dump, no credential swap, and the names from your profile.
RDP REMOTE PROOF READ (When port 3389 is open): Run whoami, hostname, ipconfig, and type the user flag in one command over RDP via NetExec.
RDP DESKTOP SCREENSHOT: Capture a PNG screenshot of the remote RDP desktop session (saved under ~/.nxc/screenshots/) to attach in Evidence -> Proof Screenshots.

actions.title: Capture the Root/Proof Flag (Windows)
actions.hypothesis: Capture the proof flag using established administrative access, or test recovered Administrator material with a remote flag attempt. Paste the result to record the access actually demonstrated. For the proof screenshot, capture the flag with hostname and ipconfig in an established session.

report.finding: Captured the root/proof flag from the Windows host.

commands.note: PREFERRED REMOTE LOCATE (Instant Desktop Sweep with NT Hash over SMB): Scans every user profile Desktop for root/proof flags using the Administrator NT hash. Finishes in under 1 second. Paste output to ungate the flag read.

commands.run: nxc winrm {{target}} -u {{dauser}} -H {{dahash}} -x 'Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users -Filter *root*.txt -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty FullName'

UNIVERSAL ON-HOST LOCATE (Works in both CMD/wmiexec/psexec/smbexec and PowerShell/Evil-WinRM): Sweep all user profile Desktops for root/proof and user/local flags in under 1 second.

commands.note: ONE-SHOT ON-HOST USER + ROOT LOCATE & PROOF READ (Works in CMD/wmiexec/psexec/smbexec and PowerShell/Evil-WinRM without needing paths first): Prints whoami, hostname, ipconfig, and every user/local and root/proof flag across all Desktops in one frame.
commands.web_note: ONE-SHOT ON-HOST USER + ROOT PROOF (Run inside your on-host shell): Prints whoami, hostname, ipconfig, and both user.txt and root.txt across all Desktops in a single screenshot frame.
commands.run: cmd /c "whoami & hostname & ipconfig & for /d %d in (C:\Users\*) do @for %f in (%d\Desktop\*user*.txt %d\Desktop\*local*.txt %d\Desktop\*root*.txt %d\Desktop\*proof*.txt) do @(echo --- %~f --- & type %~f 2>nul)"

UNIVERSAL ON-HOST PROOF READ (Works in both CMD/wmiexec/psexec/smbexec and PowerShell/Evil-WinRM): Capture whoami, hostname, ipconfig, and the ROOT/proof flag in a single command frame.

commands.web_note: COMBINED USER + ROOT PROOF READ (Inside your on-host shell): Prints whoami, hostname, ipconfig, and both {{flag_path_local}} and {{flag_path_root}} in one command.

commands.note: ON THE HOST as SYSTEM/Administrator (PowerShell / Evil-WinRM), capture the ROOT/proof flag with its identity in the same frame (whoami + hostname + ipconfig + the flag) for the report.

ON-HOST ADS LOCATE (Alternate Data Streams): Lists files and hidden alternate data streams on the Administrator Desktop. If flag files are hidden in streams (e.g. filename.txt:root.txt:$DATA), dir /r exposes them.

commands.run: Get-Item 'C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\*' -Stream * | Where-Object { $_.Stream -ne ':$DATA' } | Select-Object FileName, Stream, Length
commands.note: POWERSHELL ADS LOCATE: Enumerates NTFS alternate data streams across all files in the Administrator desktop, filtering out the default :$DATA stream.
POWERSHELL ADS READ: Reads the contents of a hidden alternate data stream flag (e.g. -Stream root.txt).
RDP REMOTE PROOF READ (When port 3389 is open): Run whoami, hostname, ipconfig, and type the root/proof flag in one command over RDP via NetExec.
RDP DESKTOP SCREENSHOT: Capture a PNG screenshot of the remote Administrator RDP desktop session (saved under ~/.nxc/screenshots/) to attach in Evidence -> Proof Screenshots.

actions.title: Post-Proof Credential & Subnet Pivot Sweep
actions.hypothesis: Capturing the proof flag is not the end of a multi-host environment: an owned host often holds dual-homed interfaces, ARP neighbors on an internal subnet, or stored credentials that unlock the next machine in the lab.
actions.proves: internal network routes, ARP neighbors, and stored host credentials from the compromised machine after proof capture
actions.does_not_prove: reachability or compromise of adjacent internal hosts until a pivot or lateral login succeeds

commands.run: ip -br addr; ip route; ip neigh; cat /etc/hosts /etc/resolv.conf 2>/dev/null
commands.note: Linux post-proof sweep: enumerate all NICs, kernel routes, ARP neighbors, and static host/DNS entries for internal pivot targets.
Windows post-proof sweep: enumerate all adapters, routing tables, ARP cache entries, and stored Credential Manager entries.
